title: 1953 AHSME Problem 47
statement: If \(x\) is greater than zero, then the correct relationship is:

solutions.text:
For \(x\gt0,\) the standard exponential inequality gives \(1+x\lt e^x.\) Taking natural logarithms yields \[ \ln(1+x)\lt x. \] If \(\log\) denotes the common logarithm, then \[ \begin{aligned} \log(1+x)&=\frac{\ln(1+x)}{\ln10}\\ &\lt\ln(1+x), \end{aligned} \] so the same listed inequality holds.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Compare \(1+x\) with an exponential function for \(x\gt0\)
The standard inequality \(\ln(1+x)\lt x\) is even stronger for common logarithms
